title: Your Pay Went Up. Your Buying Power Didn't.

scenes.vo: Average pay rose 3 percent this past year. Workers still lost ground.

captions.text: Average pay rose 3% this past year.

scenes.vo: Nominal pay is your paycheck. Real pay is what it buys.

captions.text: Real pay is what it buys.

scenes.vo: Hourly pay rose 3 percent through September. Prices rose 3.7. So real pay fell.
Say you earn 60,000. A 3 percent raise adds 1,800. Keeping up took 2,220. You're 420 short.
At your next review, compare your raise to inflation.

wageGrowth.unit: % change, average hourly earnings, all private employees
wageGrowth.source: BLS, Real Earnings — September 2026, published 2026-10-14; https://www.bls.gov/news.release/archives/realer_10142026.htm (current release page re-read 2026-11-06); also BLS Employment Situation Sep 2026, published 2026-10-02 ($37.81/hr)

cpiGrowth.unit: % change, CPI-U all items, not seasonally adjusted
cpiGrowth.source: BLS, Consumer Price Index — September 2026, published 2026-10-14; https://www.bls.gov/news.release/archives/cpi_10142026.htm; confirmed in BLS, Real Earnings — September 2026, published 2026-10-14; https://www.bls.gov/news.release/archives/realer_10142026.htm (current release page re-read 2026-11-06)

realHourly.unit: % change, real average hourly earnings, all employees
realHourly.source: BLS, Real Earnings — September 2026, published 2026-10-14; https://www.bls.gov/news.release/archives/realer_10142026.htm (current release page re-read 2026-11-06); BLS The Economics Daily, published 2026-10-20, https://www.bls.gov/opub/ted/2026/real-average-hourly-earnings-decreased-0-7-percent-from-september-2025-to-september-2026.htm. Check: 1.030/1.037 − 1 = -0.68% (rounded inputs)

exampleSalary.source: Illustrative. Raise $1,800 (3.0%), amount needed to keep pace $2,220 (3.7%), gap $420 computed in S4Real.tsx; ignores taxes

notes: Refresh check 2026-11-06: October average hourly earnings came out Nov 6 (+0.4% m/m) but October CPI and Real Earnings are not due until Nov 10, so September remains the newest matched pay-vs-prices pair.

Averages for private employees; individual raises and inflation vary. The gap is largely energy (gasoline +34.2%, core CPI +2.6% over the year). Real weekly earnings fell only 0.1% because hours rose.
